interactions.summary: The moderator thanks the audience again, calls this the first of many sessions, and invites any final comments before signoff.

Jiang thanks the moderators and audience, says he wants the live streams to become a regular and deeper practice, and frames future sessions as collaborative deep dives that can draw on community expertise in areas where he lacks knowledge.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang, with Jake's brief agreement at the end of seg-0188.

interactions.summary: The moderator agrees with the two-week plan and says the mod team will announce exact scheduling details and maintain a calendar for future events.

Jiang adds that future sessions should be recorded and uploaded for people who miss them, restates that the point is to learn together and build from one live stream to the next, and the moderator closes with thanks for the audience's boosts and participation.

speaker_notes.note: seg-0188 contains Jiang's proposal to meet again in two weeks plus the moderator's immediate assent, so it functions as a shared turn.

claims.claim: The moderator describes this livestream as the first of many future sessions.
Jiang says he wants the livestreams to become a regular practice and to go much deeper than the broad ask-me-anything format used here.
Jiang says future deep-dive sessions should draw on the expertise of the entire community, including on topics like Turkey where he openly says others know more than he does.
Jiang proposes doing the next livestream again in two weeks.
The moderator says the team will announce precise future dates and times and list events on a calendar ahead of time.
Jiang says future livestreams will be recorded and uploaded so people who cannot attend can still follow along.
Jiang says the real point of the livestream series is collective learning, where each session builds on the previous one and helps the community explore topics together.
The moderator says the audience's Discord boosts broke the viewer cap and made the event possible at scale.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang rejects the pure guru posture by using Turkey as a concrete example of a topic where he wants the audience's expertise to correct and extend him.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It keeps the community project grounded in reciprocal knowledge rather than one-way performance.

signature_moments.moment: The broad AMA is treated as only a first layer; the future ideal is collaborative workshop-style deep dives on selected topics.
signature_moments.source_phrase: really try to workshop certain ideas
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the clearest closing picture of what Jiang thinks this community can become.

signature_moments.moment: Each live stream is framed as cumulative, with the community building on top of prior sessions rather than treating them as isolated performances.
signature_moments.source_phrase: we're building on top of each live stream
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It condenses the long-term pedagogical model behind the whole experiment.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's label for the broad, non-specialized format of this first session, which he contrasts with future topic-specific deep dives.

chronology_notes.note: On 2025-10-11 Jiang ends the first livestream by sharpening its long-term design: later sessions should be regular, recorded, deeper, and more collaborative, with the community's expertise helping shape both the topics and the learning process.
